evidence_set.title: Are Appointment Reminders Allowed Under HIPAA?
evidence_set.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
evidence_set.snippet: HHS states that appointment reminders are part of treatment and may be made without a separate authorization under the HIPAA Privacy Rule.
evidence_set.supports: reminders can be part of care operations, subject to privacy safeguards

evidence_set.title: May Providers Leave Messages for Patients?
evidence_set.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
evidence_set.snippet: HHS permits patient communications by phone or mail but advises limiting message content, using professional judgment, and honoring reasonable confidential-communication requests.
evidence_set.supports: contact workflows need minimum-necessary message rules and preference handling

evidence_set.title: Patient Portal Reminder After No-Show in Ophthalmology
evidence_set.snippet: A randomized ophthalmology trial found that a portal message after a missed visit was associated with greater reattendance within the study's follow-up window than a mailed letter alone.
evidence_set.supports: recall measurement can include post-no-show reengagement by channel

evidence_set.title: Outpatient Appointment Reminder Systems and No-Shows
evidence_set.snippet: A randomized multispecialty outpatient study compared staff calls, automated reminders, and no reminders, finding different attendance and cancellation outcomes by reminder method.
evidence_set.supports: recall reporting should separate outreach method and disposition

evidence_set.title: Telephone Reminders and Kept Appointments
evidence_set.publisher: Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine
evidence_set.snippet: A randomized outpatient trial found that reminder calls changed both no-show and cancellation behavior, allowing released slots to be reused in that setting.
evidence_set.supports: recall workflow metrics should include cancellations and recovered capacity
